System Architecture Overview — “Two Worlds”

Slide 3 of 11

System Architecture — Explained

Cloud (build-time only)

  • Builder Machine ingests source PDFs (WHO, MSF, national guidelines).
  • Enriches via NVIDIA NIM chat (meta/llama-3.1-70b-instruct).
  • Embeds via NIM embed (nvidia/llama-3.2-nv-embedqa-1b-v2).
  • Indexes and signs into a signed SQLite pack.

Transport

  • Signed pack moves via USB, WiFi, or sneakernet.
  • No internet at the edge.

Edge device (runtime)

  • Pack ingested, updated atomically (verify → stage → swap with rollback).
  • Served by stdlib HTTP + SSE edge server.
  • ONNX models for embedding and reranking.

Client

  • Health worker’s phone/tablet connects via local WiFi AP to /ui/ over HTTP + SSE.

Presenter notes

“The key idea is complete separation: the cloud never touches the edge at runtime. Everything the edge needs is baked into a signed pack that arrives by physical transport. The edge device is air-gapped — zero outbound network calls.”

Slide 4 of 11

Pipeline Flow — Build-Time (3 Stages)

Slide 5 of 11

Pipeline Flow — Explained

Stage 1 — Ingest (Zero LLM)

  • Source PDFs → pdfplumber → custom geometry (headers, merged cells, bounding boxes).
  • Output: chunks + tables, then second-reader verify.
  • A table is stored as one chunk with full row/column header context.

Stage 2 — Enrich (Optional NIM)

  • Chunks → NIM chat → enriched chunks (acronyms, definitions, dosage).
  • Enrichment cache for cost control.
  • Works offline with hash-based stand-ins when NIM is unavailable.

Stage 3 — Index & Pack

  • Enriched → NIM embed → HNSW vectors + SQLite FTS5.
  • Manifest with model IDs, counts, git SHA.
  • 8 fail-closed gates → Ed25519 sign → signed pack.
  • No gate defaults to pass; release pack cannot be signed unless all gates pass.

Presenter notes

“Ingest is deliberately LLM-free — pure pdfplumber plus custom geometry. The 8 fail-closed gates are the quality gatekeeper: nothing ships unless every gate passes.”

Slide 6 of 11

Runtime Flow — Edge Device (Sequence)

Slide 7 of 11

Runtime Flow — Explained

How a question gets answered offline

  • Health worker types a question into the /ui/ test console.
  • Edge server runs hybrid search: SQLite FTS5 (BM25 keyword) + HNSW vectors (ONNX embed) in parallel.
  • Candidates go through a cross-encoder reranker (ONNX) for top-k ranking.
  • Table chunks trigger cell-level resolution with bounding boxes and highlights.
  • Verifier checks citations, dose refusal, abstention — then streams a cited answer (SSE) or returns “Not found” with a reason.

Presenter notes

“This is the critical safety path: cite or abstain. If the system can’t verify a citation or detects an unsafe dose, it refuses to answer — it never guesses. Table answers show exact cells with page-image highlights so a clinician can verify at a glance.”

Key Takeaways

Offline-First by Design

Zero external network calls at runtime. Everything arrives via signed pack over USB/WiFi/sneakernet.

Cite or Abstain

Every answer cites its source or says “not found.” No generated doses — tables verbatim only.

Fail-Closed Quality Gates

8 gates block release unless all pass. Not_run counts as failure — never defaults to pass.

Atomic Updates + Rollback

Signed packs verified with Ed25519 chain; staged in inactive slot, smoke-tested, swapped with fsync’d os.replace.
